verdict.reasoning: Patient states diarrhea for the last three days and going to the toilet 'probably like six or seven times a day' with 'loose and watery stool'.
Location and character are supported: 'in my lower abdomen...on the left side' and 'it feels, um, like a cramp...it comes and goes', consistent with left lower quadrant crampy intermittent pain.
Transcript confirms vomiting at the start that has now stopped ('I vomited at the start of the symptoms but now um I've stopped vomiting') but does not state it was only one episode.

Patient reports feeling weak and shaky and earlier subjective fever: 'i feel a bit uh weak and shaky' and 'I haven't had a fever...but I did notice um a temperature when the symptoms started, so, um, yeah around about three or four days ago.'

Patient reports loss of appetite and tolerating light foods and fluids: 'I had a loss of appetite...but I've been able to hold down fluids' and 'just soups...light foods. Like smoothies and, yeah, liquid foods mainly.'
Doctor links onset to recent takeaway and child vomiting: patient says 'I had takeaway about four days ago' at a Chinese restaurant, and 'one, um, child was vomiting, but they haven't got diarrhea.'

Patient reports asthma and that it is under control: 'other than um athsma, um I use an inhaler' and in response 'is your asthma well-controlled?' patient says 'yeah, that's fine...that's under control.'
Transcript notes inhaler use ('I use an inhaler') but does not specify salbutamol or any particular inhaler type.
Patient states 'I'm an accountant' and lives with 'my wife and two kids'.
Patient answers 'no, I don't smoke' and 'no, I I don't drink alcohol, no.'

Doctor assessment: 'it seems like you may have something, uh, called gastroenteritis...mainly caused by viruses but there can be a possibility of bacteria...I wondered whether that might be the cause' referring to Chinese takeaway, consistent with likely viral or food-borne gastroenteritis.
Asthma is described as controlled: in response to 'is your asthma well-controlled?' patient says 'yeah, that's fine...that's under control,' indicating stable asthma.
Doctor advises: 'making sure you're well hydrated, so drinking fluids' and 'there are things like Dioralyte you can get from the pharmacy...it helps replenish your minerals and vitamins.'

Doctor recommends paracetamol but without specific 1 g dose or 6-hour schedule: 'taking some paracetamol, uh, two tablets up to four times a day for the first few days can also help.' The explicit 1 g every 6 hours and 4 g max are not stated and conflict with the described dosing ('two tablets' rather than defined gram amount).
Doctor says: 'I will certainly advise you to take some time off work...I would say the next two, two to three days as the infection clears from your system to take some time off and rest.'

Follow-up advice in transcript is only: 'if your symptoms haven't got better, you know, in in three to four days, I'd like to come and see you again.' There is no mention of specific red flags like increased abdominal pain, blood in stool, persistent vomiting, or fever >38°C.

Doctor notes future investigations if ongoing: 'if it is ongoing then we have to wonder whether something else...and we may need to do further tests like um taking a sample of your stool so we can test that.' This supports consideration of stool testing if symptoms persist.
There is no explicit advice in the transcript about continuing the usual asthma inhaler; asthma medications beyond current use are not discussed in the plan.
